name: Zav/Zavah — Laws of Gonorrheal Discharge
notes: Detailed laws of the zav: counting of sightings, examination for causes, threshold between one/two/three issues, distinction from keri, relationship to sacrifice obligation

name: Examination of the Zav (Bedikat haZav)
notes: Seven factors examined to determine whether a zav's discharge was caused by an external factor (food, drink, carrying, jumping, illness, sight, thought) which would exempt him from zav status

name: Hefsek in Zav Counting (Interruption Undoing Days)
notes: Rules about how an emission of semen or additional zov during the counting period undoes previous clean days; dispute between Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel

name: Midras Tumah (Pressure/Treading Impurity)
notes: Impurity conveyed to objects fit for sitting/lying when a zav, zavah, niddah, or yoledet rests upon them; distinct from contact impurity; applies even without direct touch if weight is borne

name: Mishkav and Moshav (Objects for Lying and Sitting)
notes: Special category of objects that can become midras-defiled and in turn convey second-degree impurity to persons and garments; detailed rules about which objects qualify

name: Madaf Tumah (Impurity Above the Zav)
notes: Objects resting above a zav (even without direct contact) that become defiled at a lesser grade; the madaf conveys impurity to food and liquids

name: Zav — Impurity Through Carrying and Moving
notes: Rules distinguishing defiling through carrying (masa) vs. moving (heset) a zav; who defiles whom when zav and clean person share a moving object like a boat or animal

name: Heset (Moving/Displacing Impurity)
notes: Impurity transmitted when a zav moves an object or is moved by it, even without direct contact; distinct from touch and carrying; major topic of tractate Zavim

name: Grades of Impurity — Rishon and Sheni in Zav Context
notes: Detailed treatment of first and second degree impurity conveyed by touching/carrying a zav or objects connected to him; how separation from source affects degree; disqualification of terumah at further remove

name: Drawn Water (Mayim She'uvim) Disqualifying Immersion
notes: Rule that three logs of drawn water falling on a clean person's head and majority of body disqualifies terumah; also immersing head and majority in drawn water

name: Categories That Disqualify Terumah (Posel et haTerumah)
notes: Enumerated list of those who disqualify terumah without rendering it impure outright: eating first/second degree impure food, drinking impure liquids, tevul yom, drawn water, unwashed hands, sacred scrolls, food defiled by liquids

name: Sefer (Sacred Scroll) Defiling the Hands
notes: Rabbinic ruling that sacred scripture scrolls defile the hands; listed among those who disqualify terumah

name: Sacrifice of the Zav
notes: The obligation of a confirmed zav to bring a sacrifice after purification; threshold of three sightings required for sacrifice obligation; cases where he is exempt from sacrifice but still obligated in running water

name: Immersion of Zav in Running Water (Mayanot)
notes: Requirement for a zav to immerse specifically in running spring water (mayim chayim), not just a mikvah; applies even in intermediate cases

name: Androginus and Tumtum in Laws of Zivah
notes: Rules that androginus and tumtum bear stringencies of both male and female regarding zivah: defiled by blood like a woman and by seminal-like discharge like a man; their impurity is doubtful

name: Zav on a Balance Scale
notes: Specific case: if a zav sits on one side of a balance and objects fit for sitting are on the other side; whether the objects become defiled depends on which side outweighs the other
